statement: Two trees are given, each as: a line with n, then a line of n level-order entries where -1 marks an absent child (each placed node consumes the next two entries as its children). Print yes when the trees are identical - same shape and the same value at every position - and no otherwise. Walk both in lockstep: both empty is yes, exactly one empty is no, and otherwise the root values must match and both subtree pairs must be identical.
constraints: Node values are positive; -1 marks an absent child.

example.why: Shape and values agree at every position in the lockstep walk.

hint: Three base cases first: both empty, one empty, values differ - then recurse on both pairs.
mistake: Comparing traversal strings; different shapes can print identical sequences.
